line: Front door on Grand doesn't latch if you let it swing. Pull it till it clicks. Hollis. I'm the super for your building.
choice1: I'm {playerName}. I didn't know it did that.
choice3: I'm just here for the doctor.

line: Recycling goes out Tuesday night. Not Monday. Monday it sits in the alley and the raccoons do the sorting. Yours went out Monday.
Tuesday. Flattened. The city won't take a box with tape on it, and then it's my problem.
choice1: Why are you at the clinic?

line: It was 3B's bag. I keep a notebook. _taps his shirt pocket_
choice2: Why are you at the clinic?

line: Cut my hand on the boiler valve. They want me to have a tetanus shot. Nineteen years, this is my fourth.
choice1: Does the boiler give you trouble?

line: It's from 1962. The landlord says it has ten more winters in it. The landlord doesn't live with it. $ If the heat goes in January, tenants call me, not him. He doesn't pick up.
choice1: I'll call you if it goes.

line: Your mailbox is full. The carrier left a notice. You're 3B, the new tenant. Hollis. I'm the super.
Two of those are for the last tenant. Write 'not at this address' and put them back out. Don't throw them away. That's federal.
choice1: What happened to the last tenant?

line: Broke the lease in April. Left a cactus and three months of mail. I still get his catalogues.
Doctor says walk. I walk to the gate and back, twice, and then I go fix something.
The tenant two doors down from you. She talks. Her bike's in the stairwell again. Fire code. Tell her, since you two talk.
Your window screen's out. Third floor, left side. It came down in the wind.
Bent. I'll straighten it. Don't open that window till I do, the pigeons get in. The last tenant had pigeons.
Thursday, nine to eleven. Be there, or put a note on the door. If I come and nobody's there, it's another week.
choice2: Can I just leave you the key?

line: No. I have a key. I don't go in without a tenant there. Nineteen years, nobody's said I took anything. That's why.
Another tenant came to my door with a form from the library. Third one this month.
Proof of residence. For the library card, the clinic, the citizenship class. {usLead} sends them to me to sign, because the landlord doesn't answer. Everybody does what {usLead} says. So I sign.
I'm the super, not the landlord. My name's on forty of her forms now. If one goes wrong, it's my name. $ She's not wrong. I'd like her to call first.
The washer under the sink in 2A went. Same washer {usLead} sold me in 1998.

DeLuca. Hardware, on Fifth. That year the whole stack leaked into 2A and the ceiling came down. He says it was the pipe. It was the washer. $ I still buy from him. Everybody on Fifth does what {usLead} says, down to which washer.
He's two blocks away and he opens at seven. That's the whole reason. $ He tells people I'm the best super on Grand. I'd rather he said it was the washer.
Somebody taped the block-party flyers to the front door. Tape takes the paint off.
{usLead}'s. She asked could she put one up inside. I said the board. Somebody put it on the door. Now I've got tape on the door and a stack of flyers in five languages for a party I'm not going to.
choice2: I'll move them to the board.

line: No. I'll be fixing whatever they break. $ The board's by the mailboxes. Not the door.
{usLead} wants the alley behind Grand clear Saturday. Merchants' something.

It affects the alley. There's a blue hatchback back there with a visitor's pass for 3B. When {usLead} asks for something, the landlord calls me inside ten minutes. About the boiler he's never called me once.
Moved by Friday night. If it's there at seven, {usLead} calls the landlord, the landlord calls the tow, and then you call me. Don't call me.
A man from the city came asking for the tenant list. I told him to talk to the landlord.
choice1: What did he want it for?
choice2: Did you give it to him?

line: Didn't say. Badge and a clipboard. I don't give anybody the list. Not the city, not the census, not the church that wants to leave pamphlets. It isn't mine to give.
Pay the rent, keep the door shut, no people on the stairs. That's what I worry about. $ [worried] He came back the next day. A different man. Same clipboard.
choice1: Tell me if he comes again.

line: New city rule. Every notice in the lobby in five languages. I laminate them. Five times the laminating.
Whatever the city sends. I don't read them, I tape them. The boiler inspection notice is up in all five now, and nobody reads it in any of them.
Tenants read the one about the rent going up. Every language. That one they find.
Your packages. Four days in the hallway. You're never in.
choice1: Sorry, I've been out a lot.
choice2: Can you hold them for me?

line: I'm not a post office. The tenant in 2B signs for half the building and then complains her hallway's full. $ Pick them up tonight. After eight they go in the basement, and the basement floods.
Whenever it rains more than an inch. Last year a tenant lost a box of wedding photos down there. I'd told her. I tell everybody.
Delivery's coming at two with a part for the boiler. I have to be in 1A. You're around in the day.

_hands you a pen and a scrap of paper_ Print and sign. Write 'for Hollis, super' under it, or he takes it back to the depot and it's another week. $ Leave it inside the basement door. Don't open the box.
Water under the sink. Somebody's water. It goes down the whole stack and I find out from a ceiling. Sign for the box or don't.
No. _a pause_ It's forty pounds. Use your legs.
Hold the bottom of this. The clinic pays me to do their lights and doesn't give me a second man.
_climbs_ Both feet on the bottom rung. Don't look at your phone. $ This tube's from 2009. Nobody in this room has looked up in fifteen years.
Cash, twice a year. The landlord pays me for forty hours and I work sixty. The clinic pays for two and means it.
_comes down and folds the ladder_ Done. You can let go of it now.
The clinic's lights, the church's gutters, the bakery's grease trap. People think the super's the building. I'm the street. $ _comes down and folds the ladder_ Done. You can let go now.
